NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical nexus of AI infrastructure, depending heavily on TSMC for advanced node fabrication and SK Hynix/Micron for HBM memory while facing a near-monopoly demand pull from hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) who collectively account for the majority of data center GPU revenue. Its fabless model creates significant upstream concentration risk at TSMC, while its downstream pricing power is exceptional given the lack of near-term competitive alternatives for high-performance AI training accelerators.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a world-class systems integrator that designs its own silicon but outsources fabrication to TSMC and key components to a concentrated group of Asian suppliers, giving it significant leverage but also meaningful geographic concentration risk. On the downstream side, Apple distributes through a mix of carriers, its own retail ecosystem, and third-party platforms, while also monetizing its massive installed base through high-margin services revenue streams tied to partners like Google and major app developers.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain, depending on a small number of highly specialized equipment and materials suppliers — most notably ASML for irreplaceable EUV lithography — to manufacture chips on the world's most advanced process nodes. As the dominant pure-play foundry, TSMC serves virtually every leading fabless semiconductor designer, making it an indispensable bottleneck through which the majority of the world's advanced logic chips must flow.

On the demand side, Micron's revenue is driven by hyperscalers and device OEMs, with AI-driven HBM demand from NVIDIA emerging as a critical and fast-growing revenue vector alongside traditional mobile and cloud server memory markets.

IREN.supply_chain_summary: IREN Limited sits at the intersection of energy-intensive Bitcoin mining and high-performance AI compute infrastructure, making it critically dependent on low-cost power procurement, NVIDIA GPU supply, and robust electrical equipment vendors upstream. Downstream, IREN monetizes through Bitcoin sales on crypto exchanges (primarily Coinbase) and increasingly through selling AI compute capacity to hyperscalers and enterprise cloud customers, positioning it as a vertically integrated digital infrastructure operator.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at a nascent but strategically critical position in the advanced nuclear energy supply chain, dependent on a highly concentrated and government-regulated upstream of HALEU fuel enrichers, specialized fuel fabricators, and nuclear-grade component manufacturers. On the downstream side, Oklo is targeting AI-driven hyperscale data center operators and industrial/defense customers seeking reliable, carbon-free baseload power, though the company remains pre-revenue and all customer relationships are in LOI or early contract stages as of 2024.
